components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main operator action on a decision surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:32px; padding:0 10px; border:1px solid color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary),transparent 70%); border-radius:var(--radius-lg); background:linear-gradient(135deg,var(--primary),color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary),black 18%)); color:var(--primary-foreground); font:600 0.72rem/1.35 var(--theme-font-body); box-shadow:0 8px 24px -6px var(--accent-glow-soft); transition:filter 140ms ease-out,box-shadow 160ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter:brightness(1.1); box-shadow:0 10px 34px -6px var(--accent-glow); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(1px); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A compact supporting action that remains subordinate to the decision control.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:32px; padding:0 10px; border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:var(--radius-lg); background:var(--secondary); color:var(--secondary-foreground); font:600 0.72rem/1.35 var(--theme-font-body); transition:background 140ms ease-out,border-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--secondary),var(--foreground) 5%); border-color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary),var(--border) 55%); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform:translateY(1px); }

components.name: Assignment Field
components.description: A compact repository or issue field in the assignment row.
components.css: .ds-input { width:260px; height:32px; padding:4px 10px; border:1px solid var(--input); border-radius:var(--radius-lg); background:transparent; color:var(--foreground); font:400 0.84rem/1.4 var(--theme-font-body); transition:border-color 140ms ease-out,box-shadow 140ms ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:hover { border-color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary),var(--input) 65%); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:none; border-color:var(--ring); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch,var(--ring),transparent 50%); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A labeled status marker that never relies on color alone.
components.css: .ds-chip { --ds-tone:var(--signal-mint); display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; height:20px; padding:0 8px; border:1px solid color-mix(in oklch,var(--ds-tone),transparent 64%); border-radius:0; background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ds-tone),transparent 88%); color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ds-tone),var(--foreground) 22%); font:600 0.75rem/1 var(--theme-font-body); } .ds-chip-dot { width:7px; height:7px; border-radius:999px; background:var(--ds-tone); } .ds-chip:hover { border-color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--ds-tone),transparent 45%); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Work Card
components.description: The flat, dense unit for one work outcome and its evidence state.
components.css: .ds-work-card { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:7px; width:230px; padding:10px 11px; border:1px solid var(--hairline); border-radius:var(--radius-md); background:var(--surface); color:var(--foreground); font-family:var(--theme-font-body); transition:border-color 140ms ease-out,background 140ms ease-out; } .ds-work-card strong { font-size:0.86rem; line-height:1.35; font-weight:550; } .ds-work-card small { color:var(--muted-foreground); font-size:0.72rem; } .ds-repo { padding:1px 8px; border:1px solid var(--hairline); border-radius:0; font:400 0.72rem/1.4 var(--font-mono); } .ds-work-card:hover { border-color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary),var(--hairline) 55%); background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--surface),var(--foreground) 4%); } .ds-work-card:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Active Navigation Item
components.description: The current route, marked by text, icon, wash, and a spectral edge.
components.css: .ds-nav-active { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; width:220px; min-height:32px; padding:6px 10px; border:0; border-radius:var(--radius-md); background:linear-gradient(90deg,color-mix(in oklch,var(--signal-mint),transparent 88%),transparent 72%),var(--glass); color:var(--foreground); font:500 0.84rem/1.35 var(--theme-font-body); box-shadow:inset 1px 0 0 var(--signal-mint),inset 2px 0 0 color-mix(in oklch,var(--signal-rose),transparent 35%),inset 3px 0 0 color-mix(in oklch,var(--signal-violet),transparent 55%); } .ds-nav-active svg { width:16px; height:16px; } .ds-nav-active:hover { background:linear-gradient(90deg,color-mix(in oklch,var(--signal-mint),transparent 82%),transparent 72%),var(--glass); } .ds-nav-active:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset:2px; }

narrative.overview:
Alfred is a quiet operations field that reveals change at its edges. Neutral planes and compact typography carry the working state; narrow mint, rose, and violet signals appear only where work is active, selected, uncertain, or awaiting a decision. The result is calm enough for long sessions while keeping intervention points unmistakable.

Signal Edge is the default appearance. Category Standard maps the same semantic contract to denser graphite panels and conventional status color. Linked Fold maps it to warm paper, fine crease geometry, and gold decision accents. Theme changes may alter material, radius, and heading character, but they do not alter information architecture, control meaning, or status semantics.
keyCharacteristics: Translucent chrome around solid, legible data surfaces.
State conveyed by words, icons, dots, borders, and color together.
A restrained spectral edge reserved for changing or selected work.
Light and dark modes derived from one semantic component contract.

rules.name: The Signal-at-the-Edge Rule
rules.body: Spectral color belongs on active navigation rails, selected work, changing evidence, and status edges. Keep the data field neutral.

rules.name: The Failure Has Weight Rule
rules.body: Error red must remain distinct from mint, green, and decorative spectral color, and every error includes text or an icon.

rules.name: The Semantic Contract Rule
rules.body: All appearances consume the same background, foreground, surface, primary, border, and status roles. A theme changes expression, never meaning.

rules.name: The Evidence Voice Rule
rules.body: Use monospace only when the content is literal machine evidence. Human-readable outcomes and decisions stay in the body voice.

rules.name: The Compact Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Create hierarchy through weight, contrast, and spacing before increasing size. Operational headings remain modest.

rules.name: The Decision Rail Rule
rules.body: Evidence and approval controls occupy a dedicated inspector on wide screens and become a reachable sheet on narrow screens. They never obscure or reorder the lifecycle.

rules.name: The Chrome-Only Glass Rule
rules.body: Blur communicates persistent or overlaid chrome. Do not put long-form text directly on weak translucent material.

rules.name: The Flat Data Rule
rules.body: Cards that carry work, evidence, or metrics stay flat at rest. Hover changes border and surface tone, not elevation.

rules.name: The Structural Shape Rule
rules.body: Radius follows hierarchy: chrome may curve, dense metadata stays square, and circles are reserved for compact identity or status marks.

dos: Do use neutral surfaces for sustained reading and reserve spectral color for state edges.
Do pair every status color with a label, icon, dot, or structural change.
Do keep data cards flat and use glass only where layering has a navigational purpose.
Do preserve lifecycle order and evidence access at every breakpoint.
Do disable entry and crossfade motion when reduced motion is requested.
donts: Don't use gradients as decoration detached from status, selection, focus, or material depth.
Don't turn the interface into a metrics dashboard with oversized numbers or presentation-scale headings.
Don't use color alone to indicate approval, failure, selection, or progress.
Don't add independent theme-specific component behavior. Map new components through the shared semantic contract.
Don't place body copy on translucency that depends on backdrop blur for contrast.
